headline: Portland buys Blazers gear in a few doors. Taste lives in Old Town and the thrift bins.
summary: Nike's hometown has surprisingly few public Nike doors. Blazers volume runs through Rip City Clothing Co. at Moda Center, the west-side malls and Fred Meyer, and Oregon's lack of a sales tax pulls in shoppers from Washington. Taste comes from Old Town Chinatown and a resale circuit that Nike and adidas employees keep stocked. Nike makes every Lillard and Morant jersey but splits the shoe wall with hometown rival adidas. The pending Moda Center renovation is the opening for a year-round team store.

insights.title: Nike's hometown has few Nike doors
insights.detail: Nike Portland reopened Nov 13, 2025 at 638 SW 5th Ave after closing in late 2023, with running on its main floor. The factory store sits at Woodburn Premium Outlets, 30 miles south. The Nike Community Store on NE Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd, open since 1984 and staffed largely from Albina, closed in late 2022, and Nike said in 2023 it won't reopen. The employee store at World Headquarters in Beaverton is closed to the public. Guest passes still feed the city's resale and thrift supply.
insights.implication: Albina has had no Nike door since the NE MLK store closed. Launch Blazers-specific product with Albina partners at their venues, and use Nike Portland downtown as the Nike-run door only once it agrees to carry Blazers product. Keep the design credit and some of the proceeds in Albina.

insights.title: Tax-free Oregon pulls in Washington
insights.detail: Oregon has no sales tax. Shoppers from Vancouver and Clark County ('the Couv') cross the Columbia to buy at Jantzen Beach, Washington Square and Woodburn. The Blazers have been the only NBA team in the Pacific Northwest since the SuperSonics left Seattle in 2008, so their retail reach runs deep into Washington.
insights.implication: Plan inventory and media for a two-state market. Aim at SW Washington around Black Friday and the Woodburn outlet run, and make the tax-free price part of the pitch.

insights.title: The most Nike-literate resale market there is
insights.detail: Employee-store pickups, men's size-9 samples and archive pieces turn up at the Goodwill Outlet 'Bins' on SE Ochoco and on SE Hawthorne racks like House of Vintage. Local pickers can date a 1990s Blazers warm-up by its tag. Nike and adidas designers shop the same racks.
insights.implication: Make Portland-only exclusives scarce and archive-accurate, or this crowd will call them out. Sell limited runs by raffle through local doors and the Nike app, not in first-come lines, which resellers dominate.

insights.title: Game-day retail sits in a retail desert
insights.detail: Rip City Clothing Co. at Moda Center is the volume door for jerseys. But the Rose Quarter has little year-round street retail. Next-door Lloyd Center, once Oregon's flagship mall, has largely emptied out ahead of redevelopment. Three governments have committed $586M toward roughly $600M in Moda Center upgrades: Oregon ($365M), Multnomah County ($101M) and Portland ($120M). New owner Tom Dundon has no lease yet.
insights.implication: Use the renovation talks to push for a year-round, street-facing team store with a Nike-built basketball room. Until then, treat the arena store and the MAX ride to it as the main game-day point of sale.

insights.title: Nike wins the jersey; the shoe wall splits
insights.detail: Damian Lillard returns from his Achilles tear as an adidas athlete, and adidas runs its North American headquarters in North Portland. New arrival Ja Morant carries a Nike signature line. Every Blazers jersey is Nike-made, so Lillard's homecoming sells Nike jerseys even as his Dame line competes on the shoe wall.
insights.implication: Bet October volume on Lillard and Morant jerseys. Build Portland colorways of Morant's Nike shoe for local doors. Keep Lillard's personal marks off Nike product.

insights.title: Taste is set in Old Town, not at the malls
insights.detail: Old Town Chinatown and West Burnside hold the credibility. Compound Gallery has the limited releases, Cal Skate Skateboards the skate wall, and Deadstock Coffee the sneaker café, run by former Nike employee Ian Williams. Portland Saturday Market's maker stalls sit by the Burnside Bridge. Marcus Harvey's Portland Gear, an Instagram-born 'Portland' apparel brand, shows how far plain city pride sells here.
insights.implication: Seed city-specific product through Old Town doors first, with a paid collaboration with Portland Gear or Deadstock. Let the malls carry the restock.

insights.title: A second basketball team now shares the arena
insights.detail: The WNBA's Portland Fire began play at Moda Center in 2026. They draw on the women's-sports supporter base built around the Nike-kitted Thorns. The Fire have separate owners, so their marks are separate IP from the Blazers'. Nike still makes their uniforms under the WNBA deal.
insights.implication: Plan women's-cut Blazers product and shared-arena retail with the Fire. License Fire marks separately for any joint Rip City basketball capsule.

places.name: Rip City Clothing Co. at Moda Center
places.why: The Blazers' own retail brand, and the metro's biggest single door for jerseys and authentic product on game nights.

places.name: Pioneer Courthouse Square
places.why: 'Portland's living room' sits a block from the downtown Nike store. It's the city's default stage for brand pop-ups and watch parties.

places.name: Portland Saturday Market
places.why: A long-running weekend crafts market where local screen printers and makers sell Rip City-flavored goods. The holiday run goes to Christmas Eve.

places.name: Deadstock Coffee
places.why: Sneaker-culture coffee shop founded by ex-Nike employee Ian Williams, and a hangout and pop-up spot for the local sneaker crowd. It closed its Old Town storefront in December 2025 and now operates from the lobby café of The Hoxton hotel.

places.name: Goodwill Outlet ('the Bins')
places.why: Pay-by-the-pound bins where pickers hunt Nike samples, vintage ACG and old Blazers gear. This is the base of the local resale chain.

places.name: House of Vintage
places.why: A multi-dealer vintage mall on the Hawthorne strip, where 1980s–90s Blazers and Nike pieces are priced as archive.

places.name: Woodburn Premium Outlets
places.why: Oregon's biggest outlet center, home to a Nike Factory Store, and a tax-free destination for Washington and Canadian shoppers.

places.name: Washington Square
places.why: The metro's strongest mall, minutes from Nike's Beaverton campus. It carries the west side's athletic-chain and department-store volume.

places.name: Lloyd Center
places.why: Once Oregon's flagship mall, a MAX stop from Moda Center. Now largely vacant and slated for redevelopment, it leaves game-day retail without a neighboring district.

people.name: Marcus Harvey / Portland Gear
people.role: Founder of a Portland city-pride apparel brand
people.why: Turned an Instagram account into the city's best-known local apparel label. He's a likely collaborator for a Black-owned, Portland-made Blazers capsule.

people.name: Ian Williams / Deadstock Coffee
people.role: Former Nike employee, owner of a sneaker-culture café
people.why: His Old Town shop links Nike insiders, sneakerheads and Black Portland. That makes it a natural launch and pop-up partner.

people.name: Rip City Clothing Co.
people.role: The Trail Blazers' in-house retail brand and team store
people.why: It controls the arena door and the team's own product, so it's the partner for Nike-made Blazers volume.

people.name: Damian Lillard
people.role: Blazers guard and adidas signature athlete
people.why: His return after missing 2025-26 is the season's top jersey driver. His shoes and personal marks belong to adidas.

people.name: Ja Morant
people.role: Blazers guard and Nike signature athlete
people.why: He's Nike's first signature-line player in the Blazers' backcourt in years, and the obvious anchor for Portland colorways.

people.name: Pendleton Woolen Mills
people.why: Its wool, plaids and downtown store are Portland's heritage-textile reference. Any Blazers wool piece would run through a Pendleton license.

people.name: Fred Meyer
people.why: It carries licensed Blazers basics in neighborhood stores across the metro, so it's the everyday volume door outside the malls.

people.name: Portland Fire
people.role: WNBA team at Moda Center (2026 debut)
people.why: It adds a second basketball fanbase, mostly women's-sports supporters, to the same arena and retail calendar.

moments.name: Home opener and Lillard's return
moments.why: Lillard's first home game back after the Achilles tear, with Morant debuting, is the biggest jersey-sales night of the year at Rip City Clothing Co.

moments.name: NBA Cup night: Warriors at Trail Blazers
moments.why: Opening night of Cup group play at Moda Center is a national-TV window for Cup-specific and City Edition product.

moments.name: Black Friday tax-free weekend
moments.why: Washington shoppers stream to Woodburn, Jantzen Beach and Washington Square. It's the peak for Blazers gifting at full and outlet price.

moments.name: Portland Saturday Market holiday run
moments.why: Locals buy Portland-made gifts here, so a Nike or Blazers maker collaboration stall would sit in the right place.

moments.name: Nike Hoop Summit
moments.why: Nike's own international prospects game at Moda Center (in recent years) is a home-turf moment for Nike Basketball product.

moments.name: Portland Fire season
moments.why: It keeps the Moda Center team store and women's basketball product busy through the Blazers' off-season.

moments.name: Good in the Hood
moments.why: A long-running multicultural festival in NE Portland's King neighborhood. It's a natural Albina pop-up moment.

moments.name: 1977 championship 50th anniversary
moments.why: Fifty years since Portland's only NBA title: a once-only reason for archive-accurate reissues at every door.

vocabulary.meaning: Bill Schonely's broadcast call, now the city's nickname and the name of the team's retail arm, Rip City Clothing Co.
The Blazers' logo: five stripes against five, for two teams of five players.
What many locals still call Moda Center, its name from 1995 to 2013.
Vancouver, Washington, just across the Columbia. Its residents shop in tax-free Oregon.
The Goodwill Outlet on SE Ochoco, where pickers dig for Nike samples and vintage team gear.
Nike's staff store at the Beaverton campus, and the passes employees hand to friends. It's a local status marker and a resale source.
Nike World Headquarters in Beaverton. Locals in the industry also just say 'campus'.
Oregon's standing retail selling point, posted at outlets and repeated by every cross-river shopper.

designCues.cue: Blazers red as the anchor, run tonal (red on red) on retail exclusives so they read different from the arena-store jerseys
designCues.source: The Trail Blazers' official red, the color of the pinwheel and of every Rip City Clothing Co. wall
designCues.use: Tonal hoodies and warm-ups for Portland-only doors. Keep standard red and black for core licensed product.

designCues.cue: A register-receipt hangtag and interior print reading 'SALES TAX $0.00 / RIP CITY'
designCues.source: Oregon's lack of a sales tax, and the Washington shoppers who cross the Columbia for it
designCues.use: Hangtags and inside-neck prints on Portland-exclusive product sold at Moda Center, Woodburn and Nike Portland. Locals and the Couv both get the joke.

designCues.cue: Interior spec stamp in the style of a Nike sample label, with the Moda Center ZIP code and the release date instead of the word 'sample'
designCues.source: The employee-store and sample culture of Nike's hometown, and the Bins pickers who hunt samples
designCues.use: An insider detail inside Portland-only pieces. It nods to sample culture without misleading resale buyers about authenticity.

designCues.cue: Pinwheel stripe tape: five red and five black bars repeated down a side seam
designCues.source: The 1970 pinwheel logo, five players against five
designCues.use: Track-pant and sleeve tape on retail-exclusive warm-ups. It's an NBA-licensed mark Nike can use as outfitter.

designCues.cue: Wool-flannel board-shirt plaid in Blazers red and black
designCues.source: Pendleton Woolen Mills, Portland's heritage textile maker
designCues.use: A licensed Pendleton x Blazers overshirt or blanket in plaids and solids. Skip Indigenous trade-blanket motifs unless Native designers are commissioned.

designCues.cue: Washed, slightly faded 1990s warm-up finish with era-accurate neck tags
designCues.source: The Hawthorne vintage racks and Bins pickers who date old Blazers gear by the tag
designCues.use: Archive reissues for the 1977 50th anniversary and the Drexler era, matched exactly to the originals. This market will check.

productHooks: Albina First: a Blazers x Nike capsule co-designed with credited, paid Albina artists. It launches at an Albina partner venue a week before wide release, with part of the proceeds going to local youth basketball.
'SALES TAX $0.00' Rip City tee and hoodie, sold at Moda Center, Nike Portland and the Woodburn factory store and marketed to the Couv and SW Washington.
A Portland colorway of Morant's Nike signature shoe in Blazers red and black, raffled through Old Town doors and Nike Portland. Add a Deadstock Coffee launch night, after brand-safety sign-off.
1977 50th-anniversary archive reissue (warm-up and shooting shirt), dropped June 5, 2027 by raffle at Rip City Clothing Co. and Nike Portland. Build it to the original specs.
A licensed Portland Gear x Blazers collaboration, sold as a pop-up at Pioneer Courthouse Square and the Saturday Market.
watchouts: Lillard is an adidas athlete, and adidas is a North Portland neighbor. Keep 'Dame Time', 'Dame D.O.L.L.A.' and his personal logo off Nike product. NBA-licensed name-and-number jerseys are fine.

Pendleton's best-known blankets draw on Native American designs. Use plaids and solids, or commission Native designers who are credited and paid. Never lift Indigenous motifs, and treat Pendleton as licensed third-party IP.

The Albina corridors (MLK, Williams, Alberta, Mississippi) are gentrified historic Black neighborhoods. Launches there need investment in long-time Black residents and businesses, not just a backdrop.
Downtown and Lloyd Center retail has thinned since 2020. Check foot traffic and door health before betting a flagship launch on downtown or the Rose Quarter.
Portland Gear, Deadstock Coffee, Compound Gallery and Portland Fire marks are third-party IP and need licenses. Any Morant-led launch needs Nike brand-safety review, given his 2023 suspensions.

sources.title: Rose Quarter / Moda Center (official venue site)

districts.name: Downtown core (Pioneer Courthouse Square, SW Broadway, Pioneer Place)
districts.profile: The historic shopping core around Pioneer Courthouse Square, with Nike Portland, Nordstrom, Columbia and Pendleton flagships. The Pioneer Place mall has lost many tenants since 2020.
districts.shopper: Tourists, conventioneers, office workers in a slower-recovering downtown, and Washington day-trippers shopping tax-free.

districts.name: Old Town–Chinatown and West Burnside
districts.profile: A small, credible sneaker and skate cluster (Compound Gallery, Cal Skate, Deadstock Coffee) beside the Saturday Market and the Burnside Bridge.
districts.shopper: Sneakerheads, skaters, artists, and the Nike and adidas designers who set taste for everyone else.

districts.name: Albina corridors (NE MLK Jr. Blvd, N Williams, NE Alberta, N Mississippi)
districts.profile: Historic Black Portland, now heavily gentrified. It lost its Nike door when the Community Store on MLK closed in 2022. It's lined with independent shops, Alberta's Last Thursday street fair and Good in the Hood.
districts.shopper: Long-time Black families and youth hoopers alongside newer, more affluent residents.

districts.name: Rose Quarter and Lloyd District
districts.profile: Moda Center and its team store, Veterans Memorial Coliseum and a largely vacant Lloyd Center. It's a MAX hub with little year-round street retail.
districts.shopper: Game-night and concert crowds arriving by MAX, plus Portland Fire fans in summer.

districts.name: SE Hawthorne and Belmont
districts.profile: Portland's vintage and thrift strip (House of Vintage, Red Light Clothing Exchange, Buffalo Exchange). The Goodwill Outlet Bins are farther south on SE Ochoco.
districts.shopper: Vintage pickers, students, creatives and resellers digging for Nike samples and old Blazers gear.

districts.name: Washington Square and the Beaverton corridor
districts.profile: Tigard's top-grossing regional mall, with athletic chains, Nordstrom and Lids. It's minutes from Nike World Headquarters and its employee store.
districts.shopper: West-side suburban families and the Nike, Intel and tech-campus workforce.

districts.name: Clackamas Town Center
districts.profile: An east-side regional mall in Happy Valley off I-205, with the athletic-chain and Lids assortment for Clackamas County.
districts.shopper: East-side and suburban families and high-school athletes buying team basics and jerseys.

districts.name: Woodburn Premium Outlets
districts.profile: Oregon's largest outlet center, on I-5 30 miles south, with a Nike Factory Store and the region's tax-free outlet tourism.
districts.shopper: Washington and Canadian day-trippers, tour groups and value-hunting Willamette Valley families.

doors.name: Rip City Clothing Co. (Moda Center team store)
doors.why: The Blazers' own retail brand and highest-volume jersey door. It anchors Lillard, Morant and City Edition sales, and it's the place to push for a year-round store in the renovation.

doors.name: Nike Portland (downtown)
doors.why: Reopened Nov 13, 2025 at 638 SW 5th Ave after a two-year closure, with running on its main floor. Whether it carries Blazers or Nike Basketball product is unconfirmed.

doors.name: Nike Factory Store, Woodburn Premium Outlets
doors.why: The metro's tax-free outlet volume door for Nike and Blazers basics, heavily shopped by Washington visitors.

doors.name: Nike Employee Store (World Headquarters)
doors.why: Closed to the public, but its guest passes and staff purchases feed Portland's resale and thrift supply and its insider status culture.

doors.name: Compound Gallery
doors.why: Portland's long-standing sneaker, streetwear and gallery boutique for limited releases. It's the natural tier door for a Portland colorway.

doors.name: Cal Skate Skateboards
doors.why: A decades-old Portland skate shop that carries skate footwear and connects the city's skate scene to any Blazers x SB idea.

doors.name: Deadstock Coffee
doors.why: A sneaker-themed café from ex-Nike employee Ian Williams, working as a community hub and a pop-up and launch venue. It closed its Old Town storefront in December 2025 and now operates from the lobby café of The Hoxton hotel.

doors.name: Portland Gear
doors.why: The city-pride apparel brand with the biggest local following. A licensed collaboration would carry street credibility.

doors.name: Pendleton Woolen Mills (downtown store)
doors.why: Portland's heritage wool brand, and the licensing route to a credible Blazers wool overshirt or blanket.

doors.name: House of Vintage
doors.why: A multi-dealer vintage mall where archive Blazers and Nike pieces show which eras the market values.

doors.name: Goodwill Outlet ('the Bins')
doors.why: The base of Portland's Nike-sample and vintage-Blazers resale chain, and a gauge of how scarce exclusives really are.

doors.name: Foot Locker and Lids (Washington Square, Clackamas Town Center)
doors.why: The suburban volume doors for Morant footwear, jerseys and caps.

doors.name: Fred Meyer
doors.why: The Portland-founded chain where everyday fans pick up licensed Blazers tees and hats with the groceries.
